subject: PrivDep DPA: BYOK boundaries, operator telemetry, and subprocessors (Medica Consult)
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@medica-consult.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Compliance Team <compliance@medica-consult.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment questions: BYOK, operator access, and subprocessors

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the private-deploy overview on Friday. Our procurement and compliance teams had a few follow-ups after reviewing the materials:

- We need confirmation that customer-controlled keys (BYOK) are supported with no escrow requirement and that Redwood operators cannot decrypt customer model input or outputs.
- Please clarify the exact subprocessors that will have network-level access during on-prem/VPC deploys (e.g., monitoring/backup partners).
- What operator telemetry do you collect from private deployments? We need an explicit list and retention windows for logs/metrics.
- Any cross-border transfer clauses we should flag in the DPA for our EU patients?

I've attached a short questionnaire (medica_privacy_qs.xlsx) and the compliance team would like an initial written response before we proceed to legal redlines.

Can you route this to the right folks internally? Goal is to have answers + a redline-ready DPA by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Alice
--
Alice Martin
Head of Compliance, Medica Consult
alice.martin@medica-consult.com
Attachment: medica_privacy_qs.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@medica-consult.com>
Cc: Compliance Team <compliance@medica-consult.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: BYOK, operator access, and subprocessors

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Irene (legal), Karthik (security), and Marcus (infra) to provide authoritative answers. High-level response while they draft details:

- BYOK: Supported in VPC and on-prem packages. Customer keys remain customer-controlled; Redwood does not require key escrow for standard Private deployments. There are documented breakglass procedures for incident response that can be constrained in the DPA (we can make operator activation an auditable, customer-approved workflow).
- Subprocessors: For Private (VPC/on-prem) we limit subprocessors to a short list; for hosted we use broader cloud partners. Marcus will enumerate the specific partners used for monitoring/backup/patching in customer-managed VPCs.
- Telemetry: We collect runtime health metrics, GPU/host-level resource metrics, and crash traces necessary for debugging; we do not collect customer prompt/content payloads for Private deployments. Retention windows are negotiable; default is 90 days for metrics and 365 days for control-plane audit logs.
- Cross-border transfers: We support region-restricted deployments and can add a DPA clause to restrict any operator access/telemetry exports outside the specified region.

I'll follow up with the redline and a proposed supplemental DPA paragraph for BYOK and operator activation controls by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Neha
--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: BYOK, operator access, and subprocessors

Hi all — quick legal read on the BYOK/operator items. I attached inline language in the redline that addresses the two primary concerns:

1) Key custody: We will accept customer-provided CMKs and document that Redwood personnel have no access to plaintext keys. We will include an explicit clause that operators may not export or reconstruct customer keys except via a mutually-agreed emergency process that requires: (a) written approval from Medica, (b) two-person internal approval at Redwood (legal + infra), and (c) a time-limited access token that is logged.

2) Operator access scope: Propose we define a narrow "operator role" in the DPA that enumerates allowed scopes (instance health, orchestration status, agent liveness). Any ask beyond that (e.g., memory/core dumps that could contain plaintext) requires a separate SOW and customer consent.

3) Subprocessors: We'll provide the short list Marcus will confirm. Add an obligation to notify Medica 30 days before adding any new subprocessor for Private deployments. This can be stricter than hosted.

I'm marking a few redlines as negotiable; please review and call out anything you need tightened.

Thanks,
Irene
--
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
Attachment: draft_dpa_medica_redline.docx (redline with inline comments)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alice Martin <alice.martin@medica-consult.com>, Compliance Team <compliance@medica-consult.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: BYOK, operator access, and subprocessors

Adding technical detail on telemetry and operator artifact access:

- Telemetry collected (private deployments):
  * Metrics: CPU/GPU utilization, queue lengths, latencies, memory pressure (aggregate only) — default retention 90 days.
  * Control-plane audit logs: user/operator API calls, deploy/rollout events, authentication events — retention 365 days.
  * Crash dumps: core/gpu traces are retained only if a customer opt-in or if the customer marks a support bundle for explicit upload; they are not automatically shipped.

- Content/exposure guarantees: Runtime request/response payloads are never included in telemetry for Private deployments unless explicit debug mode is enabled by the customer and a scoped support ticket is opened.

- Operator tooling: Operators can open a "support session" that generates a session token and records a video/text transcript of actions. We can add an enforcement point in the DPA that requires customer approval for any support session that includes elevated privileges.

- Subprocessors: In on-prem scenarios we do not run managed backups unless the customer requests Redwood-managed backup; when we do, the backup partner is a named subprocessor and encryption-at-rest keys remain customer-managed.

I'll confirm the partner names with Marcus and include them in the redline.

Thanks,
Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: BYOK, operator access, and subprocessors

Hi all — partner & infra specifics as requested. Attaching a simplified diagram (infra_diagram.png) for clarity. Short list of third parties that may be subprocessors for Private/VPC installs when customers opt-in:

- Monitoring: LogStreamOps LLC (metrics ingestion only; no payloads), default retention controlled by customer.
- Backup/restore (opt-in): VaultArc Backup Services (encrypted artifacts; keys customer-provided).
- Managed patching (optional): SecurePatch Inc. (has access to instance-level endpoints but not application payloads).

Operational notes:
- We do not ship customer keys to any third party. Customer CMKs remain in customer-managed KMS or HSM.
- Breakglass: The breakglass workflow is a written runbook requiring customer POA/approval and two internal approvals; all actions are logged and a signed post-incident report is produced.
- Evidence we can provide: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), penetration test summaries, and sample audit logs for the control plane.

Next steps I suggest: (1) Neha to send the updated redline with the operator-role language Irene suggested, (2) schedule a 30-min technical call with Karthik/Marcus/Alice to walk through the infra diagram and telemetry retention, (3) legal (Thomas/Irene) to exchange DPA redlines after call.

Regards,
Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
